fields.description:
Define a versioned synthetic/deidentified fixture corpus and characterization strategy for existing PDFs across statements, invoices, correspondence, and reports. Capture expected input behavior and preservation constraints before remediation changes.

## Batch-three A/B rollup

This parent tracks two distinct children: `dap-jo9.2.1.2` authors the two pre-spike financial-table fixtures and independent baselines; `dap-jo9.2.1.3` expands the remediation corpus only after `dap-jo9.1.6.4` records a finite feasibility disposition and only against evidenced capabilities and accepted profiles. Keep statements, invoices, correspondence, and reports in remediation coverage. The closed metadata-manifest task `dap-jo9.2.1.1` remains historical planning metadata; its planned rows do not mean fixture artifacts exist. A fixture plan, corpus row, or machine pass is not a repair or release result.

## Proposed v3 increment placement

The separate v3 source/baseline qualification work is proposed as one narrowly bounded task under this fixture-plan parent; no new ID, issue, edge, or artifact is created by this text. Keep dap-jo9.2.1.2 closed as historical pre-spike evidence and dap-jo9.2.1.3 open for broader four-family evidence-bounded expansion. Preserve this parent's complete rollup and broad profile prerequisite. The owner must approve the exact prerequisite split before a first-pair execution path can bypass broader unfinished profile/corpus work; planning text does not satisfy or remove those blockers.

fields.acceptance_criteria:
After the accepted bounded feasibility disposition in dap-jo9.1.6.4, expand only against evidenced capabilities, accepted profiles, support boundaries, and independently observable expectations. Retain all four remediation families and explicit unsupported/ambiguous rows. Do not gate on universal font, language, or topology breadth. Keep generation separate; feasibility disposition is not eligible-candidate evidence, and fixture plans are not repair or conformance evidence.

Given a family has no accepted capability/profile evidence, when refining its corpus coverage, then retain an explicit unsupported, deferred, or decision-blocked coverage record with evidence and owner question; do not invent a fixture, drop correspondence/report obligations, or present a planned row as executed coverage. The first financial pair and proposed separate v3 qualification do not close this cross-family expansion task.

Contract tests cover the smallest consumed input/profile, candidate operation/output, evidence, and error/result interface for the bounded remediation consumer. Retain valid/invalid, deterministic evidence, cancellation/timeout, applicable idempotence, unsupported capability, tool failure, and license-policy cases. Keep dependencies permissively licensed, preserve the CI-only veraPDF exception, and add no enterprise-only component, speculative generic worker API, general workflow framework, writer selection, or runtime exception.

Given the actual bounded pair consumer and accepted prerequisites, when defining its contract, then show each field/result is consumed and cover exact input identity, explicit operator-confirmed operation, separate output identity, preservation evidence, classified failure, and cancellation/deadline behavior. Given an invalid, ambiguous, unsupported, canceled, timed-out, partial, or audit-failed operation, then no successful candidate is exposed. Candidate/evidence schema determinism does not assert byte-deterministic PDF serialization. FN-REM-INTAKE, FN-REM-CHARACTERIZE, FN-REM-REPAIR-BASELINE, FN-REM-COMPARE, and FN-REM-VALIDATE-OUTPUT remain requirement responsibilities, not a mandate for separate packages, services, or APIs. Preserve dap-jo9.1.6.4 and dap-jo9.1.3 as prerequisites; no writer/runtime selection is made.

As a proposed authorized document submitter, I want a supported existing PDF assessed and a bounded structural repair applied with a preservation record, so that the resulting document can enter review without altering the source. The role name and authority boundary are provisional and require domain validation.

## First increment and full-story boundary

US-REM-001 / CAP-REM-PRESERVE is the stable story/capability mapping in docs/traceability/catalog.json and docs/traceability/matrix.md. The conceptual feature is operator-confirmed financial-table repair with preservation evidence; it is a planning grouping, not a new Beads issue type. The first implementation increment is the equal-priority synthetic statement/invoice pair, under the separately approved v3 source/baseline plan. Keep all six canonical cases and their owner dap-jo9.2.3.1: statement, invoice, correspondence, report, malformed, and fidelity. Correspondence/report and remaining whole-task malformed/fidelity scope remain outstanding later increments. First-pair success, Reject, or Inconclusive does not complete this story or dap-jo9.2.3.2.

fields.acceptance_criteria:
After the exact PR #50 full raw reports/contracts are durably retained through an authorized handoff and all findings are independently assessed, write failing tests first and implement the separately reviewed first increment: only the bounded paired statement/invoice candidate path. Keep historical v1/v2 fixtures and hashes immutable; separately version and hash any new inputs, repaired baselines, fonts, or resources. Require explicit operator confirmation of each target table-header mapping before repair; no unconfirmed or automatic association is applied. Use only exact reviewed dependencies/resources with permissive licenses and provenance. For each family, preserve input bytes and exact displayed strings; assert intended association and order; independently compare structure, text extraction, and rendered output; and validate the exact candidate hash with explicit candidate-bound `ua2`. Exercise incorrect, ambiguous, missing, malformed, unsafe, and unsupported mappings; cancellation, timeout, output cap, partial-write, and audit-failure paths; rejected evidence never becomes success. First-increment success requires both statement and invoice candidates to receive completed COMPLIANT candidate-bound assessment and all first-increment acceptance controls to pass, but that pair result does not close this whole task. If the bounded pair cannot meet this, stop with an evidence-backed unsupported/reject/inconclusive result and a next decision; do not widen the pair or close other obligations.

Retain all six linked case obligations across the full task: statement, invoice, correspondence, report, malformed-input behavior, and fidelity/preservation. Correspondence and report require their own separately reviewed future increment boundaries and accepted executable evidence. The first increment's malformed/fidelity controls do not close any remaining whole-task obligations for those cases; define and review any later boundaries before implementation. Pair success, Reject, or Inconclusive cannot close this task. Close the whole task only after accepted executable evidence satisfies every acceptance obligation for all six cases, including correspondence/report and full malformed/fidelity scope. Keep canonical case ownership and dependencies unchanged. This does not select a production writer, claim general PDF support, or satisfy human semantic/AT authority or release gates. Shared engineering definition of done: see `docs/requirements/definition-of-done.md`.

Given separately approved and independently qualified v3 positive baselines for both families, when the exact proposed writer performs positive no-op controls before damaged inputs are opened, then preserve the accepted financial/text/structure/render/resource oracle and require completed candidate-bound explicit-ua2 COMPLIANT reports with zero failed rules/checks for both positive and no-op outputs. Given a damaged input derived only by its named row-two /Headers change, when the operator explicitly confirms that exact mapping, then produce a separate hash-bound repaired candidate; the relationship oracle must reject the wrong association even if the machine validator passes it. Given either family fails any first-increment control, then stop with precise evidence and no pair-success claim. All six original full-task obligations, every existing dependency, canonical case ownership, and broader unsupported boundaries remain unchanged. v1/v2 bytes and findings are immutable; no v3 source/resource/value choice is approved by this refinement.

1. An eligible candidate produced per the recorded eligibility standard, with hash-bound evidence.
2. Or: the eligibility standard recorded as the open blocker with owner and date.

The second numbered alternative above records an open blocker only and cannot satisfy candidate-production acceptance or authorize closing this task. Given an owner-accepted eligibility standard and actual candidate bytes, when the candidate is assessed against that standard, then retain exact candidate/hash-bound preservation and explicit-ua2 evidence and demonstrate every required criterion. Given the standard, candidate, or required evidence is missing, rejected, inconclusive, or unverifiable, then keep candidate production blocked and do not close this task. Eligibility for entering human/AT review must be distinguished from the eventual genuine human/AT acceptance required to close dap-jo9.2.5.9; do not make each depend on the other's completion.

fields.notes:
2026-10-13 v2 gate clarification: acceptance of `dap-jo9.1.6.4` may enable bounded contract implementation after other prerequisites, but is not eligible-candidate evidence. This issue stays open until an actual eligible candidate has accepted preservation evidence and a valid completed COMPLIANT explicit-ua2 assessment bound to its hash, plus genuine authorized semantic and AT records under the accepted protocol. Noncompliant findings, processing errors, simulations, and generic CI do not satisfy the candidate requirement; assess findings against the bounded operation, and unexplained regressions or contradictions block a feasibility Proceed. Disclosed fixture limitations remain classified. Missing or rejected human approval continues to block release.

2026-10-14 panel (deferred): define a semantic carve-out for byte-change invalidation, or confirm invalidation-by-design per the hash-bound-evidence constraint. Domain decision.
2026-10-14 PR #71 P1 role-authority blocker: the approver persona is accepted, but no trusted source proves that an identity held that role at reviewed_at. New decision task dap-jo9.1.1.6 defines the open source and temporal-policy choice; this task now depends on it. Until accepted source/validity semantics are recorded, do not implement role verification or infer authority from an identity string. See docs/requirements/reviewer-evidence-verification.md. Existing .1.1.4/.1.1.5 history and actual eligible-candidate closure requirements remain intact.
2026-10-14 review-boundary correction for PR #72 finding https://github.com/pratik-saptarshi/document-accessibility-pipeline/pull/72#discussion_r4277453114: preserved the roadmap readiness boundary by splitting labeled synthetic contract work into dap-jo9.2.5.9.1 and source-dependent role verification into dap-jo9.2.5.9.2. Only .9.2 depends on dap-jo9.1.1.6; the parent depends on both child slices for completion. The contract task retains the existing authority/protocol, candidate, feasibility, and case prerequisites; simulations remain non-evidence.
2026-10-14 completion/readiness graph correction for PR #72: independent contract and role tasks have no scheduling parent-child edge; the parent tracks synthetic-contract work and has an explicit blocking dependency on the role-verification task. Role verification blocks on both the contract task and open authority decision dap-jo9.1.1.6. This avoids parent-child/block mixed-edge propagation while keeping the role source in the gate-completion path. A copied Beads database verified readiness; no real prerequisite statuses were changed.

2026-10-17 proposed product refinement: dap-jo9.2.5.2 is closed for specification ownership only. It is not a genuine human/AT pass and must not be reopened solely to execute this gate. Given an eligible exact candidate and authoritative time-valid reviewer evidence under dap-jo9.1.1.6 / dap-jo9.2.5.9.2, when authorized people perform the accepted protocol, then record separate genuine semantic and AT outcomes bound to the candidate and machine evidence. Given missing authority or review evidence, then remain blocked/review-needed. Preserve dap-jo9.2.5.9.1's labeled-simulation boundary and existing dependencies. This text is proposed and unapplied.
